targets.old_statement: Shared middle lanes welcome left turns from both flows all day, while reversible middles lend the whole lane to one rush-hour tide at a time under arrow and X lamps.
targets.old_spoken_statement: Shared middle lanes welcome left turns from both flows all day, while reversible middles lend the whole lane to one rush-hour tide at a time under arrow and X lamps.
targets.statement: Shared center lanes are reserved for left turns and permitted U-turns by traffic from both directions—though some become reversible lanes during rush hours—whereas reversible lanes carry traffic one way at certain times and the opposite way at other times under lane-control signs and lights.

targets.old_statement: Stop lines fix where wheels must halt for signs and lamps, crosswalks fence where feet may roam with the right of way, and each duty survives even where paint is missing.
targets.old_spoken_statement: Stop lines fix where wheels must halt for signs and lamps, crosswalks fence where feet may roam with the right of way, and each duty survives even where paint is missing.
targets.statement: Stop lines mark where your vehicle must stop before reaching the line for a sign or signal, while crosswalks define where pedestrians cross and require yielding to pedestrians in or about to enter them, including unmarked crosswalks at intersections.

targets.old_statement: At a HAWK beacon, steady red requires drivers to stop while pedestrians cross. Flashing red also requires a full stop; drivers may then proceed when the crosswalk is clear and travel is safe, as with an ordinary flashing red light.
targets.old_spoken_statement: At a HAWK beacon, steady red requires drivers to stop while pedestrians cross. Flashing red also requires a full stop; drivers may then proceed when the crosswalk is clear and travel is safe, as with an ordinary flashing red light.
targets.statement: At a HAWK signal, solid red means pedestrians are in the crosswalk and motorists must stop, whereas flashing red means the signal is about to deactivate and drivers must stop but may proceed once pedestrians have cleared the crosswalk.
